correctness.rationale: The rook line graph of selected bipartite edges is a union of cliques exactly when all nontrivial edge components are stars. Covering both shores suffices for maximality because an omitted edge would join two components, giving a component containing disjoint edges. Leaving vertices uncovered on both shores fails maximality. If just one shore has uncovered vertices, a star centered on the other shore or a single-edge component would be extendible; the only maximal possibilities are stars of at least two edges centered on the shore with uncovered vertices. Labeled role selection, independent leaf partitions, and the bijection pairing single-edge endpoints give exactly the factorial and Stirling factors. This includes the singleton-shore cases. In the gap regime the spanning types have two through m components at most, so size lies from n to n+m−2. The given constructions realize each size, and the two opposite-center stars are the only maximum type for m≥3. Independent enumeration and formula computations agreed on seven small boards, including singleton-shore and gap-regime cases.
residual_risks: The replay is finite corroboration only. The general classification and counting proof supply the all-board result.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Rook graphs with at least two rows and columns have diameter two. A triple on a geodesic is exactly an induced P₃ transited from endpoint to endpoint; hence general position equals the cluster condition, and maximality agrees. The earlier cluster result directly includes the singleton-shore cases too.

originality.rationale: The earlier Resultary cluster record states the identical all-board labeled maximal-cluster census in equivalent EGF form, plus the same maximum coefficient and a broader exact support theorem. Another earlier record already gives the classification and spectrum under the equivalent general-position predicate. The frozen restricted-regime gap and Stirling form do not add a distinct finding.
